name: 4Square
description: Fill the Hole: a Kempe-swap puzzle game about the Four Colour Theorem

paragraphs: A mobile puzzle game about the Four Colour Theorem. A map is coloured with four elements so that neighbours differ; one region, the hole, is left blank because its five neighbours use all four. Your move is a Kempe swap: pick a chain of regions that alternate two elements and swap them. Get the rim down to three elements and the hole can be filled.

Play: (also open index.html; it is a static site, no build needed to play). It is a progressive web app: the 📲 Install button on the title screen adds it to an Android or iPhone home screen, where it runs full screen and offline (manifest.webmanifest, sw.js; icons from tools/makeicons.py).

The levels come from real research data: maps from an exhaustive census of sphere triangulations, with locked "π loops", 66666 six-rings and the deepest known start (6 swaps). Levels 19.1-21.3 add the four-colour proof search's own hard pieces (the degree-7 arrangement R and the degree-8 binder of October 2026) grown into full maps, padded maps (classic pits wrapped in outer bands that add decoy chains but never shorten the way out), and the two combined (see "Hurdle and padded maps" below). The game grew out of GraphColourDeductiveSolver (site). The Four Colour Theorem is already proved;…
